newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb on Russian train kills three, injures seven.
newsitem.headline: Bomb on Russian train kills three, injures seven.

text.p: Three people were killed and seven injured on Friday when an explosion ripped through a train travelling from Moscow to St Petersburg in what officials said could have been a suicide bombing.
"It was a bomb which was hidden in the toilets of one of the carriages," an emergencies ministry official told Reuters.
He said the incident happened at around 6:30 p.m. (1430 GMT) on train number 24 near Torbino station in the Novgorod region northwest of Moscow.
About four hours later the train arrived in St Petersburg. Television pictures showed two people with bandaged heads being led by medical staff to waiting ambulances.

Interfax news agency quoted an emergency ministry official as saying that, according to preliminary investigations, the blast was the work of an unidentified suicide bomber. A 13-year-old boy and another man also died, the agency said.
The ministry's duty officer declined to confirm the report, which he said came from investigators. No other officials were immediately available for comment.
Interfax said the damaged carriage had been uncoupled at the site of the blast and the four most seriously wounded were taken to a nearby hospital.
Railways Minister Nikolai Aksenenko was among officials and security police who headed for the site of the crash, Russian television said.
Bomb blasts are fairly common in Russia, where explosives are often used in contract killings of businessmen.
Earlier this year, four people were killed in explosions at two different railway stations in southern Russia.
Moscow blamed those blasts on Chechen rebels, but separatist leaders in the southern republic, torn by a 21-month conflict with Russian troops which ended last August, denied any involvement.
Last year four people were killed in a bombing on the Moscow metro and dozens were injured in blasts on two trolleybuses in the capital.
